        head += struct.pack('<H', 0)                 # reserved
        assert len(head)==280, len(head)
        sblob=bytearray()
        for s in inst.samples:
            flags = 0x10 if s.panning is not None else 0
            if s.loop_length>1: flags |= 1
            if s.loop_type=='pingpong': flags |= 2
            slen=len(s.data)
            name=(s.name.encode('ascii','replace')[:22]).ljust(22,b' ')
            sh = struct.pack('<I', 18+4+22+1+1+1+2+4+4+4+1+1+1+1+4)  # sample header size = 48 (0x30)
            sh = struct.pack('<I', 0x30)
            sh += name
            sh += struct.pack('<BBB', s.loop_type=='pingpong' and 1 or 0, 0, 0)  # type? -> fixed below
            # rebuild properly
            sh = struct.pack('<I', 0x30) + name
            sh += struct.pack('<B', 16 if slen>32767 else 0)     # sample type: 16 = 16 bit
            sh += struct.pack('<b', s.finetune)
            sh += struct.pack('<B', s.volume)
            sh += struct.pack('<B', s.relative & 0xFF)
            sh += struct.pack('<B', flags)
            sh += struct.pack('<I', s.loop_start)
            sh += struct.pack('<I', s.loop_length)
            sh += struct.pack('<f', float(s.c4spd))
            sh += struct.pack('<I', 0)   # sample data pointer (unused)
            sblob += sh
            sblob += np.asarray(s.data, dtype='<i2').tobytes()
        ins_blob.append(bytes(head)+bytes(sblob))
    # ---- module header ----
    hdrlen=276
    h=bytearray()
    h += b'Extended Module: '
    h += (title.encode('ascii','replace')[:20]).ljust(20,b' ')
    h += b'\x1a'
    h += b'FastTracker II v2.08'
    h += struct.pack('<H', 0x0104)
    h += struct.pack('<I', hdrlen)
    h += struct.pack('<H', len(orders))
    h += struct.pack('<H', restart)
    h += struct.pack('<H', nchannels)
    h += struct.pack('<H', npat)
    h += struct.pack('<H', len(instruments))
    h += struct.pack('<H', 0)
    h += struct.pack('<B', speed)
    h += struct.pack('<B', globalvol)
    h += struct.pack('<H', 0)
    ol = bytearray(orders)
    ol += bytes(256-len(orders))
    h += ol
    assert len(h)==60+hdrlen, len(h)
    out=bytes(h)
    for p in pat_blob: out += p
    for i,b in enumerate(ins_blob):
        b = struct.pack('<I', len(b)) + b[4:]
        out += b
    return out

cd /workspace && cat > work/roundtrip.py <<'EOF'
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/workspace/work')
from f2 import call
import numpy as np, wave
SR=44100
# build module with known cells
call('module_new',{'channels':3,'name':'RT'})
call('sample_load',{'path':'/workspace/work/a440b.wav','instrument':1,'sample':0})
call('sample_set',{'instrument':1,'sample':0,'volume':64,'panning':80,'loop_start':441,'loop_length':10000,'flags':1,'finetune':3,'relative_note':57})
call('instrument_set',{'instrument':1,'name':'RTINST'})
call('pattern_set_length',{'pattern':0,'rows':48})
call('pattern_set_cell',{'pattern':0,'row':0,'channel':0,'note':61,'instrument':1,'volume':70})
call('pattern_set_cell',{'pattern':0,'row':5,'channel':1,'note':73,'instrument':1,'volume':64,'effect':0x0A,'effect_param':0x04})
call('pattern_set_cell',{'pattern':0,'row':10,'channel':2,'note':97})
call('pattern_set_cell',{'pattern':0,'row':12,'channel':0,'note':0,'instrument':0,'volume':0,'effect':0x41,'effect_param':0x08})
call('pattern_set_length',{'pattern':1,'rows':16})
call('pattern_set_cell',{'pattern':1,'row':3,'channel':1,'note':64,'instrument':1,'volume':50})
call('order_set',{'position':0,'pattern':0}); call('order_set',{'position':1,'pattern':1})
call('song_set',{'bpm':160,'speed':4,'length':2,'loop_start':1,'global_volume':60})
print('info before', call('module_info',{})[0])
call('module_save',{'path':'/workspace/work/rt.xm'})
print('save ok')
# render before load
call('module_render',{'path':'/workspace/work/rt_before.wav','rate':44100,'bits':16,'amp':16})
call('module_load',{'path':'/workspace/work/rt.xm'})
print('info after load', call('module_info',{})[0])
for (p,r,c) in [(0,0,0),(0,5,1),(0,10,2),(0,12,0),(1,3,1)]:
    print(p,r,c,call('pattern_get_cell',{'pattern':p,'row':r,'channel':c})[0])
print('pat len p1', call('pattern_set_length',{'pattern':1,'rows':16}) )
call('module_render',{'path':'/workspace/work/rt_after.wav','rate':44100,'bits':16,'amp':16})
def loadf(p):
    ww=wave.open(p); d=np.frombuffer(ww.readframes(ww.getnframes()),dtype='<i2').astype(float)/32768
    return d, ww.getnframes()
a,na=loadf('work/rt_before.wav'); b,nb=loadf('work/rt_after.wav')
print('frames',na,nb,'identical', np.array_equal(a,b) if na==nb else 'len differ')
print('peak',np.abs(a).max(),np.abs(b).max())
EOF
python3 work/roundtrip.py

{"command": "cd /workspace && cat > work/xmdec.py <<'EOF'
import struct
def decode_pat(b, off, nrows, nchan):
    """standard XM pattern unpacking; returns rows of (note,ins,vol,eff,par)"""
    p=off; rows=[]
    for r in range(nrows):
        packs=b[p]; p+=1
        row=[(0,0,0,0,0)]*nchan
        ch=0
        for k in range(packs):
            hdr=b[p]; p+=1
            if hdr & 0x80:
                ch=b[p]; p+=1
            else:
                if hdr==0:
                    # end of row packing? (some writers use 0 pad)
                    pass
            cell=row[ch] if ch < nchan else (0,0,0,0,0)
            nt,ins,vol,ef,ep=cell
            if hdr & 0x01: nt=b[p]; p+=1
            if hdr & 0x02: ins=b[p]; p+=1
            if hdr & 0x04: vol=b[p]; p+=1
            if hdr & 0x08: ef=b[p]; p+=1
            if hdr & 0x10: ep=b[p]; p+=1
            if ch < nchan: row[ch]=(nt,ins,vol,ef,ep)
            ch+=1
        rows.append(row)
    return rows, p
b=open('work/tmpl.xm','rb').read()
hdrlen=struct.unpack_from('<I',b,60)[0]
off=60+hdrlen
plen,nrows,nchan,psize=struct.unpack_from('<IBHH',b,off) if False else (None,)*4
# standard pattern header: length(4) packtype(1) nrows(2) patsize(2)
hlen=struct.unpack_from('<I',b,off)[0]
ptype=b[off+4]; nr=struct.unpack_from('<H',b,off+5)[0]; nc=struct.unpack_from('<H',b,off+7)[0]; ps=struct.unpack_from('<H',b,off+9)[0]
print('pat hlen',hlen,'ptype',ptype,'rows',nr,'chan',nc,'patsize',ps)
rows,p=decode_pat(b,off+hlen,nr,nc)
print('consumed',p-(off+hlen),'expected',ps)
for i,r in enumerate(rows[:6]): print(i,r)
EOF
python3 work/xmdec.py"}

import struct
def decode_pat(b, off, nrows, nchan):
    """standard XM pattern unpacking; returns rows of (note,ins,vol,eff,par)"""
    p=off; rows=[]
    for r in range(nrows):
        packs=b[p]; p+=1
        row=[(0,0,0,0,0)]*nchan
        ch=0
        for k in range(packs):
            hdr=b[p]; p+=1
            if hdr & 0x80:
                ch=b[p]; p+=1
            else:

            if ch < nchan: row[ch]=(nt,ins,vol,ef,ep)

"""Write a standard FastTracker II 2.00 XM file (uncompressed patterns)."""
import struct, numpy as np

def cell(note=0, ins=0, vol=0, eff=0, par=0):
    return (note, ins, vol, eff, par)

class Env:
    def __init__(self, pts=(), sus=(0,1), loop=(0,1), sustain=False, loopy=False):
        self.pts=list(pts); self.sus=sus; self.loop=loop
        self.sustain=sustain; self.loopy=loopy
    @property

class Sample:
    def __init__(self, name, data, loop_start=0, loop_length=0, pingpong=False,
                 volume=64, panning=None, relative=57, c4spd=8363.0, finetune=0):
        self.name=name
        self.data=np.asarray(data,dtype='<i2')
        self.loop_start=loop_start; self.loop_length=loop_length
        self.pingpong=pingpong
        self.volume=volume
        self.panning=panning          # 0..255, None -> not present (old instrument)
        self.relative=relative; self.c4spd=c4spd; self.finetune=finetune

class Instrument:
    def __init__(self, name, samples=(), keymap=None, venv=None, penv=None,
                 vib_type=1, vib_sweep=0, vib_depth=0, vib_rate=0, volfade=60):
        self.name=name; self.samples=list(samples)
        if keymap is None:
            keymap=[(1 if self.samples else 0)]*96
        self.keymap=list(keymap)
        self.venv=venv or Env(); self.penv=penv or Env()
        self.vib_type=vib_type; self.vib_sweep=vib_sweep
        self.vib_depth=vib_depth; self.vib_rate=vib_rate
        self.volfade=volfade

def _env_chunk(env):
    out=struct.pack('<H', len(env.pts))
    for p in env.pts:
        out += struct.pack('<HH', int(p[0]), int(p[1]))
    return out

def _instrument(inst):
    body=bytearray()
    body += (inst.name.encode('ascii','replace')[:22]).ljust(22,b'\x00')
    body += struct.pack('<B', 0)              # type
    body += struct.pack('<H', len(inst.samples))
    body += bytes(inst.keymap[:96])
    body += _env_chunk(inst.venv)
    body += _env_chunk(inst.penv)
    body += struct.pack('<B', 0)              # num volume loop points (legacy byte)
    body += struct.pack('<B', 0)              # num panning loop points (legacy byte)
    body += struct.pack('<BB', *inst.venv.sus)
    body += struct.pack('<BB', *inst.venv.loop)
    body += struct.pack('<BB', *inst.penv.sus)
    body += struct.pack('<BB', *inst.penv.loop)
    body += struct.pack('<B', inst.venv.dtype)
    body += struct.pack('<B', inst.penv.dtype)
    body += bytes(18)                          # dummy: 16 MIDI-PCM mapping + 2 ?
    body += bytes(6)                           # unused
    body += struct.pack('<BBBB', inst.vib_type, inst.vib_sweep, inst.vib_depth, inst.vib_rate)
    body += struct.pack('<H', inst.volfade)
    body += struct.pack('<H', 0)               # reserved
    assert len(body)==276, len(body)
    head=struct.pack('<I', 0)                  # header length placeholder (0x169=361)
    sblob=bytearray()
    for s in inst.samples:
        flags = (0x10 if s.panning is not None else 0) | (1 if s.loop_length>1 else 0) | (2 if s.pingpong and s.loop_length>1 else 0)
        sh=struct.pack('<I',0x30)
        sh += (s.name.encode('ascii','replace')[:22]).ljust(22,b'\x00')
        sh += struct.pack('<B', 16)            # sample type: 16 bit
        sh += struct.pack('<b', s.finetune)
        sh += struct.pack('<B', s.volume)
        sh += struct.pack('<B', s.relative)
        sh += struct.pack('<B', flags)
        sh += struct.pack('<I', s.loop_start)
        sh += struct.pack('<I', s.loop_length)
        if s.panning is None:
            sh += struct.pack('<B', 255)       # 'right' (old pan)

        sh += struct.pack('<I', 0)             # sample data pointer
        sblob += sh + s.data.tobytes()

    # note: standard is length(4) packtype(1) nrows(2) nchan(2) patsize(2) = 11 bytes
    hdr=struct.pack('<IBHHH', 9, 0, nrows, nchan, len(data))
    return hdr+bytes(data)

def build(title, orders, patterns, instruments, nchannels, speed=6, bpm=125,
          restart=0, globalvol=64):
    out=bytearray()
    out += b'Extended Module: '
    out += (title.encode('ascii','replace')[:20]).ljust(20,b' ')
    out += b'\x1a'
    out += b'Python XM writer  '
    out += struct.pack('<H', 0x0104)
    out += struct.pack('<I', 276)
    out += struct.pack('<H', len(orders))
    out += struct.pack('<H', restart)
    out += struct.pack('<H', nchannels)
    out += struct.pack('<H', len(patterns))
    out += struct.pack('<H', len(instruments))
    out += struct.pack('<H', 0)
    out += struct.pack('<B', speed)
    out += struct.pack('<B', globalvol)
    out += struct.pack('<H', 0)
    ol=bytearray(orders); ol += bytes(256-len(orders))
    out += ol
    assert len(out)==60+276, len(out)
    for p in patterns: out += _pattern(p)
    for i in instruments: out += _instrument(i)
    return bytes(out)

    hdr=struct.pack('<IBHHH', 9, 0, nrows, nchan, len(data))

def build(title, orders, patterns, instruments, nchannels, speed=6, bpm=125,
          restart=0, globalvol=64):
    out=bytearray()
    out += b'Extended Module: '
    out += (title.encode('ascii','replace')[:20]).ljust(20,b' ')
    out += b'\x1a'
    out += b'Python XM writer  '
    out += struct.pack('<H', 0x0104)
    out += struct.pack('<I', 276)
    out += struct.pack('<H', len(orders))
    out += struct.pack('<H', restart)
    out += struct.pack('<H', nchannels)
    out += struct.pack('<H', len(patterns))
    out += struct.pack('<H', len(instruments))
    out += struct.pack('<H', 0)
    out += struct.pack('<B', speed)
    out += struct.pack('<B', globalvol)
    out += struct.pack('<H', 0)
    ol=bytearray(orders); ol += bytes(256-len(orders))
    out += ol
    assert len(out)==60+276, len(out)
    for p in patterns: out += _pattern(p)
    for i in instruments: out += _instrument(i)
    return bytes(out)

"""Standard FastTracker II 2.00 XM writer (uncompressed patterns, 16-bit samples)."""
import struct, numpy as np

def cell(note=0, ins=0, vol=0, eff=0, par=0):
    return (note, ins, vol, eff, par)
EMPTY = cell(0,0,0,0,0)

class Env:
    def __init__(self, pts=(), sus=(0,0), loop=(0,0), sustain=False, loopy=False):
        self.pts=list(pts); self.sus=sus; self.loop=loop
        self.sustain=sustain; self.loopy=loopy
    @property
    def dtype(self):
        return (1 if self.pts else 0) | (2 if self.loopy else 0) | (4 if self.sustain else 0)

class Sample:
    def __init__(self, name, data, loop_start=0, loop_length=0, pingpong=False,
                 volume=64, panning=None, relative=57, c4spd=8363.0, finetune=0):
        self.name=name
        self.data=np.asarray(data,dtype='<i2')
        self.loop_start=loop_start; self.loop_length=loop_length
        self.pingpong=pingpong; self.volume=volume
        self.panning=panning; self.relative=relative
        self.c4spd=float(c4spd); self.finetune=finetune

class Instrument:
    def __init__(self, name, samples=(), keymap=None, venv=None, penv=None,
                 vib_type=1, vib_sweep=0, vib_depth=0, vib_rate=0, volfade=60):
        self.name=name; self.samples=list(samples)
        if keymap is None:
            self.keymap=[(1 if self.samples else 0)]*96
        else:
            self.keymap=list(keymap)
        self.venv=venv or Env(); self.penv=penv or Env()
        self.vib_type=vib_type; self.vib_sweep=vib_sweep
        self.vib_depth=vib_depth; self.vib_rate=vib_rate
        self.volfade=volfade

def _env_chunk(env):
    out=struct.pack('<H', len(env.pts))
    for (x,y) in env.pts:
        out += struct.pack('<HH', int(x)&0xFFFF, int(y)&0xFFFF)
    return out

def _instrument(inst):
    hdr=bytearray()
    hdr += (inst.name.encode('ascii','replace')[:22]).ljust(22,b'\x00')
    hdr += struct.pack('<B', 0)
    hdr += struct.pack('<H', len(inst.samples))
    hdr += bytes(inst.keymap[:96])                                  # 96
    hdr += _env_chunk(inst.venv)
    hdr += _env_chunk(inst.penv)
    hdr += struct.pack('<BB', 0, 0)                                 # n vol loop, n pan loop (legacy)
    hdr += struct.pack('<BB', *inst.venv.sus)
    hdr += struct.pack('<BB', *inst.venv.loop)
    hdr += struct.pack('<BB', *inst.penv.sus)
    hdr += struct.pack('<BB', *inst.penv.loop)
    hdr += struct.pack('<BB', inst.venv.dtype, inst.penv.dtype)
    hdr += bytes(18)                                                # dummy 16 midi-pcm map + 2? 
    hdr += bytes(6)                                                 # unused
    hdr += struct.pack('<BBBB', inst.vib_type, inst.vib_sweep, inst.vib_depth, inst.vib_rate)

"""Standard FastTracker II 2.00 XM writer (uncompressed patterns, 16-bit samples)."""
import struct, numpy as np

def cell(note=0, ins=0, vol=0, eff=0, par=0):
    return (note, ins, vol, eff, par)
EMPTY = cell(0,0,0,0,0)

class Env:
    def __init__(self, pts=(), sus=(0,0), loop=(0,0), sustain=False, loopy=False):
        self.pts=list(pts); self.sus=sus; self.loop=loop
        self.sustain=sustain; self.loopy=loopy
    @property
    def dtype(self):
        return (1 if self.pts else 0) | (2 if self.loopy else 0) | (4 if self.sustain else 0)

class Sample:
    def __init__(self, name, data, loop_start=0, loop_length=0, pingpong=False,
                 volume=64, panning=None, relative=57, c4spd=8363.0, finetune=0):
        self.name=name
        self.data=np.asarray(data,dtype='<i2')
        self.loop_start=loop_start; self.loop_length=loop_length
        self.pingpong=pingpong; self.volume=volume
        self.panning=panning; self.relative=relative
        self.c4spd=float(c4spd); self.finetune=finetune

class Instrument:
    def __init__(self, name, samples=(), keymap=None, venv=None, penv=None,
                 vib_type=1, vib_sweep=0, vib_depth=0, vib_rate=0, volfade=60):
        self.name=name; self.samples=list(samples)
        if keymap is None:
            self.keymap=[(1 if self.samples else 0)]*96
        else:
            self.keymap=list(keymap)
        self.venv=venv or Env(); self.penv=penv or Env()
        self.vib_type=vib_type; self.vib_sweep=vib_sweep
        self.vib_depth=vib_depth; self.vib_rate=vib_rate
        self.volfade=volfade

def _env_chunk(env):
    out=struct.pack('<H', len(env.pts))
    for (x,y) in env.pts:
        out += struct.pack('<HH', int(x)&0xFFFF, int(y)&0xFFFF)
    return out

def _instrument(inst):
    hdr=bytearray()
    hdr += (inst.name.encode('ascii','replace')[:22]).ljust(22,b'\x00')
    hdr += struct.pack('<B', 0)
    hdr += struct.pack('<H', len(inst.samples))
    hdr += bytes(inst.keymap[:96])                                  # 96
    hdr += _env_chunk(inst.venv)
    hdr += _env_chunk(inst.penv)
    hdr += struct.pack('<BB', 0, 0)                                 # n vol loop, n pan loop (legacy)
    hdr += struct.pack('<BB', *inst.venv.sus)
    hdr += struct.pack('<BB', *inst.venv.loop)
    hdr += struct.pack('<BB', *inst.penv.sus)
    hdr += struct.pack('<BB', *inst.penv.loop)
    hdr += struct.pack('<BB', inst.venv.dtype, inst.penv.dtype)
    hdr += bytes(18)                                                # dummy 16 midi-pcm map + 2? 
    hdr += bytes(6)                                                 # unused
    hdr += struct.pack('<BBBB', inst.vib_type, inst.vib_sweep, inst.vib_depth, inst.vib_rate)
    hdr += struct.pack('<H', inst.volfade)
    hdr += struct.pack('<H', 0)
    # header length field = 4 (this field) + len(hdr)  ... standard: 0x169 = 361 when no env points
    hlen = 4 + len(hdr)
    body=struct.pack('<I', hlen) + bytes(hdr)
    sb=bytearray()
    for s in inst.samples:
        flags=(0x10 if s.panning is not None else 0) | (1 if s.loop_length>1 else 0) | (2 if (s.pingpong and s.loop_length>1) else 0)
        sh=struct.pack('<I', 0x30)
        sh += (s.name.encode('ascii','replace')[:22]).ljust(22,b'\x00')
        sh += struct.pack('<B', 16)
        sh += struct.pack('<b', s.finetune)
        sh += struct.pack('<B', s.volume)
        sh += struct.pack('<B', s.relative)
        sh += struct.pack('<B', flags)
        sh += struct.pack('<I', s.loop_start)
        sh += struct.pack('<I', s.loop_length)
        if s.panning is None:
            sh += struct.pack('<B', 255) + bytes(3)
        sh += struct.pack('<f', s.c4spd)
        sh += struct.pack('<I', 0)
        sb += sh + s.data.tobytes()
    return body+bytes(sb)

def _pattern(rows, nchan):
    nrows=len(rows)
    data=bytearray()
    for row in rows:
        data.append(0)
        for r in range(nchan):
            (nt,ins,vol,ef,ep) = row[r] if r < len(row) else EMPTY
            data += bytes([nt&0xFF, ins&0xFF, vol&0xFF, ef&0xFF, ep&0xFF])
    hdr=struct.pack('<IBBHH', 9, 0, 0, nrows, nchan)   # length, packtype, (reserved byte)-> rows high? 
    hdr=struct.pack('<IBBHHH', 9, 0, 0, nrows, nchan, len(data))
    return bytes(hdr)+bytes(data)

def build(title, orders, patterns, instruments, nchannels, speed=6, bpm=125,
          restart=0, globalvol=64):
    out=bytearray()
    out += b'Extended Module: '
    out += (title.encode('ascii','replace')[:20]).ljust(20,b' ')
    out += b'\x1a'
    out += b'Python XM writer  '
    out += struct.pack('<H', 0x0104)
    out += struct.pack('<I', 276)
    out += struct.pack('<H', len(orders))
    out += struct.pack('<H', restart)
    out += struct.pack('<H', nchannels)
    out += struct.pack('<H', len(patterns))
    out += struct.pack('<H', len(instruments))
    out += struct.pack('<H', 0)
    out += struct.pack('<B', speed)
    out += struct.pack('<B', globalvol)
    out += struct.pack('<H', 0)
    ol=bytearray(orders); ol += bytes(256-len(orders))
    out += ol
    assert len(out)==336, len(out)
    for p in patterns: out += _pattern(p, nchannels)
    for i in instruments: out += _instrument(i)
    return bytes(out)

                 volume=64, panning=None, relative=57, c4spd=8363.0, finetune=0):
        self.name=name
        self.data=np.asarray(data,dtype='<i2')
        self.loop_start=loop_start; self.loop_length=loop_length
        self.pingpong=pingpong; self.volume=volume
        self.panning=panning; self.relative=relative
        self.c4spd=float(c4spd); self.finetune=finetune

class Instrument:
    def __init__(self, name, samples=(), keymap=None, venv=None, penv=None,
                 vib_type=1, vib_sweep=0, vib_depth=0, vib_rate=0, volfade=60):
        self.name=name; self.samples=list(samples)
        if keymap is None:
            self.keymap=[(1 if self.samples else 0)]*96
        else:
            self.keymap=list(keymap)
        self.venv=venv or Env(); self.penv=penv or Env()
        self.vib_type=vib_type; self.vib_sweep=vib_sweep
        self.vib_depth=vib_depth; self.vib_rate=vib_rate
        self.volfade=volfade

def _env_chunk(env):
    out=struct.pack('<H', len(env.pts))
    for (x,y) in env.pts:
        out += struct.pack('<HH', int(x)&0xFFFF, int(y)&0xFFFF)
    return out

def _instrument(inst):
    hdr=bytearray()
    hdr += (inst.name.encode('ascii','replace')[:22]).ljust(22,b'\x00')
    hdr += struct.pack('<B', 0)
    hdr += struct.pack('<H', len(inst.samples))
    hdr += bytes(inst.keymap[:96])                                  # 96
    hdr += _env_chunk(inst.venv)
    hdr += _env_chunk(inst.penv)
    hdr += struct.pack('<BB', 0, 0)                                 # n vol loop, n pan loop (legacy)
    hdr += struct.pack('<BB', *inst.venv.sus)
    hdr += struct.pack('<BB', *inst.venv.loop)
    hdr += struct.pack('<BB', *inst.penv.sus)
    hdr += struct.pack('<BB', *inst.penv.loop)
    hdr += struct.pack('<BB', inst.venv.dtype, inst.penv.dtype)
    hdr += bytes(18)                                                # dummy 16 midi-pcm map + 2? 
    hdr += bytes(6)                                                 # unused
    hdr += struct.pack('<BBBB', inst.vib_type, inst.vib_sweep, inst.vib_depth, inst.vib_rate)
    hdr += struct.pack('<H', inst.volfade)
    hdr += struct.pack('<H', 0)
    # header length field = 4 (this field) + len(hdr)  ... standard: 0x169 = 361 when no env points
    hlen = 4 + len(hdr)
    body=struct.pack('<I', hlen) + bytes(hdr)
    sb=bytearray()
    for s in inst.samples:
        flags=(0x10 if s.panning is not None else 0) | (1 if s.loop_length>1 else 0) | (2 if (s.pingpong and s.loop_length>1) else 0)
        sh=struct.pack('<I', 0x30)
        sh += (s.name.encode('ascii','replace')[:22]).ljust(22,b'\x00')
        sh += struct.pack('<B', 16)
        sh += struct.pack('<b', s.finetune)
        sh += struct.pack('<B', s.volume)
        sh += struct.pack('<B', s.relative)
        sh += struct.pack('<B', flags)
        sh += struct.pack('<I', s.loop_start)
        sh += struct.pack('<I', s.loop_length)
        if s.panning is None:
            sh += struct.pack('<B', 255) + bytes(3)
        sh += struct.pack('<f', s.c4spd)
        sh += struct.pack('<I', 0)
        sb += sh + s.data.tobytes()
    return body+bytes(sb)

def _pattern(rows, nchan):
    nrows=len(rows)
    data=bytearray()
    for row in rows:
        data.append(0)
        for r in range(nchan):
            (nt,ins,vol,ef,ep) = row[r] if r < len(row) else EMPTY
            data += bytes([nt&0xFF, ins&0xFF, vol&0xFF, ef&0xFF, ep&0xFF])
    hdr=struct.pack('<IBBHH', 9, 0, 0, nrows, nchan)   # length, packtype, (reserved byte)-> rows high? 
    hdr=struct.pack('<IBBHHH', 9, 0, 0, nrows, nchan, len(data))
    return bytes(hdr)+bytes(data)

def build(title, orders, patterns, instruments, nchannels, speed=6, bpm=125,
          restart=0, globalvol=64):
    out=bytearray()
    out += b'Extended Module: '
    out += (title.encode('ascii','replace')[:20]).ljust(20,b' ')
    out += b'\x1a'
    out += b'Python XM writer  '
    out += struct.pack('<H', 0x0104)
    out += struct.pack('<I', 276)
    out += struct.pack('<H', len(orders))
    out += struct.pack('<H', restart)
    out += struct.pack('<H', nchannels)
    out += struct.pack('<H', len(patterns))
    out += struct.pack('<H', len(instruments))
    out += struct.pack('<H', 0)
    out += struct.pack('<B', speed)
    out += struct.pack('<B', globalvol)
    out += struct.pack('<H', 0)
    ol=bytearray(orders); ol += bytes(256-len(orders))
    out += ol
    assert len(out)==336, len(out)
    for p in patterns: out += _pattern(p, nchannels)
    for i in instruments: out += _instrument(i)
    return bytes(out)

"""Standard XM 2.00 writer with proper pattern compression."""
import struct, numpy as np

OFF = 97   # note off
NONE = 0

class Env:
    def __init__(self, pts=(), sus=(0,0), loop=(0,0), sustain=False, loopy=False):
        self.pts=[(int(x),int(y)) for x,y in pts]; self.sus=sus; self.loop=loop
        self.sustain=sustain; self.loopy=loopy
    @property
    def dtype(self):
        return (1 if self.pts else 0)|(2 if self.loopy else 0)|(4 if self.sustain else 0)

class Sample:
    def __init__(self,name,data,loop_start=0,loop_length=0,pingpong=False,volume=64,
                 panning=None,relative=57,c4spd=8363.0,finetune=0):
        self.name=name; self.data=np.asarray(data,dtype='<i2')
        self.loop_start=loop_start; self.loop_length=loop_length; self.pingpong=pingpong
        self.volume=volume; self.panning=panning; self.relative=relative
        self.c4spd=float(c4spd); self.finetune=finetune

class Instrument:
    def __init__(self,name,samples=(),keymap=None,venv=None,penv=None,
                 vib_type=1,vib_sweep=0,vib_depth=0,vib_rate=0,volfade=60):
        self.name=name; self.samples=list(samples)
        self.keymap=list(keymap) if keymap is not None else [(1 if self.samples else 0)]*96
        self.venv=venv or Env(); self.penv=penv or Env()
        self.vib_type=vib_type; self.vib_sweep=vib_sweep; self.vib_depth=vib_depth
        self.vib_rate=vib_rate; self.volfade=volfade

def _env(e):
    out=struct.pack('<H',len(e.pts))
    for x,y in e.pts: out+=struct.pack('<HH',x,y)
    return out

def _instr(inst):
    h=bytearray()
    h+=(inst.name.encode()[:22]).ljust(22,b'\x00')
    h+=struct.pack('<B',0)+struct.pack('<H',len(inst.samples))
    h+=bytes(inst.keymap[:96])
    h+=_env(inst.venv)+_env(inst.penv)
    h+=struct.pack('<BB',0,0)
    h+=struct.pack('<BB',*inst.venv.sus)+struct.pack('<BB',*inst.venv.loop)
    h+=struct.pack('<BB',*inst.penv.sus)+struct.pack('<BB',*inst.penv.loop)
    h+=struct.pack('<BB',inst.venv.dtype,inst.penv.dtype)
    h+=bytes(18)+bytes(6)
    h+=struct.pack('<BBBB',inst.vib_type&0xFF,inst.vib_sweep&0xFF,inst.vib_depth&0xFF,inst.vib_rate&0xFF)
    h+=struct.pack('<H',inst.volfade)+struct.pack('<H',0)
    body=struct.pack('<I',4+len(h))+bytes(h)
    sb=bytearray()
    for s in inst.samples:
        flags=(0x10 if s.panning is not None else 0)|(1 if s.loop_length>1 else 0)|(2 if s.pingpong and s.loop_length>1 else 0)
        sh=struct.pack('<I',0x2F+1)          # 48
        sh+=(s.name.encode()[:22]).ljust(22,b'\x00')
        sh+=struct.pack('<B',16)+struct.pack('<b',s.finetune)+struct.pack('<B',s.volume)+struct.pack('<B',s.relative)
        sh+=struct.pack('<B',flags)+struct.pack('<I',s.loop_start)+struct.pack('<I',s.loop_length)
        if s.panning is None: sh+=struct.pack('<B',255)+bytes(3)
        sh+=struct.pack('<f',s.c4spd)+struct.pack('<I',0)
        assert len(sh)==48, len(sh)
        sb+=sh+s.data.tobytes()
    return body+bytes(sb)

def pack_pattern(rows, nchan):
    """rows: list of nrows lists of (note,ins,vol,eff,par) per channel (len nchan)"""
    out=bytearray()
    for row in rows:
        for c in range(nchan):
            note,ins,vol,ef,ep = row[c]
            if note in (None,0) and ins==0 and vol==0 and ef==0 and ep==0:
                out.append(0x20)          # empty channel
                continue
            f=0x80
            if note is not None and note!=NONE: f|=1
            if ins: f|=2
            if vol: f|=4
            if ef: f|=8
            if ep: f|=0x10
            out.append(f)
            if f&1: out.append((note if note!=97 else 97)&0xFF)
            if f&2: out.append(ins&0xFF)
            if f&4: out.append(vol&0xFF)
            if f&8: out.append(ef&0xFF)
            if f&0x10: out.append(ep&0xFF)
        out.append(0x00)                  # end of row
    hdr=struct.pack('<IBBHHH',9,0,len(rows),nchan,min(len(out),65535))
    return hdr+bytes(out)

def build(title, orders, patterns, instruments, nchannels, speed=6, bpm=125, restart=0, globalvol=64):
    assert all(len(r)==nchannels for p in patterns for r in p), 'row width mismatch'
    o=bytearray()
    o+=b'Extended Module: '
    o+=(title.encode()[:20]).ljust(20,b' ')
    o+=b'\x1a'+b'xmstd writer     '
    o+=struct.pack('<H',0x0104)+struct.pack('<I',276)
    o+=struct.pack('<H',len(orders))+struct.pack('<H',restart)
    o+=struct.pack('<H',nchannels)+struct.pack('<H',len(patterns))+struct.pack('<H',len(instruments))
    o+=struct.pack('<H',0)+struct.pack('<BB',speed,globalvol)+struct.pack('<H',0)
    ol=bytearray(orders); ol+=bytes(256-len(orders)); o+=ol
    assert len(o)==336,len(o)
    for p in patterns: o+=pack_pattern(p,nchannels)
    for i in instruments: o+=_instr(i)
    return bytes(o)
PYEOF

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/workspace/work')
from f2 import call
import numpy as np, wave
SR=44100
def render(cells,rows=32,spd=3,bpm=150):
    call('module_new',{'channels':1,'name':'arp2'})
    call('sample_load',{'path':'/workspace/work/c132.wav','instrument':1,'sample':0})
    call('sample_set',{'instrument':1,'sample':0,'volume':64,'panning':128,'loop_start':2000,'loop_length':15000,'flags':1})
    call('pattern_set_length',{'pattern':0,'rows':rows})
    call('song_set',{'bpm':bpm,'speed':spd,'length':1})
    for c in cells:
        call('pattern_set_cell',{'pattern':0,'channel':0,'row':c['row'],'note':c.get('note',0),'instrument':c.get('instrument',0),
            'volume':c.get('volume',0),'effect':c.get('effect',0),'effect_param':c.get('effect_param',0)})
    call('module_render',{'path':'/workspace/work/arp2.wav','rate':SR,'bits':16,'amp':16})
    ww=wave.open('work/arp2.wav'); d=np.frombuffer(ww.readframes(ww.getnframes()),dtype='<i2').astype(float)/32768
    st=d.reshape(-1,2)
    return (st[:,0]+st[:,1])/2, SR*spd*2.5/bpm
def dom_semi(x,st,dur,f0=132.0):
    s=x[int(st):int(st+dur)]
    if len(s)<dur*0.6 or np.abs(s).max()<0.02: return np.nan
    N=len(s); sp=np.abs(np.fft.rfft(s*np.hanning(N))); fr=np.fft.rfftfreq(N,1/SR)
    band=(fr>f0*0.5)&(fr<f0*8)
    sp=sp*band
    i=int(np.argmax(sp))
    return 12*np.log2(fr[i]/f0)
for lbl,cells in [('arp 0x00/0x07',[{'row':0,'note':61,'instrument':1,'volume':64,'effect':0x00,'effect_param':0x07}]),
                  ('arp 0x00/0x0C',[{'row':0,'note':61,'instrument':1,'volume':64,'effect':0x00,'effect_param':0x0C}]),
                  ('arp 0x00/0x03',[{'row':0,'note':61,'instrument':1,'volume':64,'effect':0x00,'effect_param':0x03}]),
                  ('arp 0x00/0x070C',[{'row':0,'note':61,'instrument':1,'volume':64,'effect':0x00,'effect_param':0x7C}]),
                  ('arp 0x10/0x07',[{'row':0,'note':61,'instrument':1,'volume':64,'effect':0x10,'effect_param':0x07}]),
                 ]:
    x,rl=render(cells,rows=24,spd=3)
    tk=[dom_semi(x,(r+k/3)*rl+20, rl/3*0.8) for r in range(8,16) for k in range(3)]
    print(f'{lbl:16s}', ' '.join('  .  ' if v!=v else f'{v:5.2f}' for v in tk))
EOF

import numpy as np
SR=44100
def f_of_note(n): return 440.0*2**((n-69)/12)

def harm_wave(F, T, partials, phase_j=0.13):
    """partials: list of (harmonic_index, amplitude)"""
    t=np.arange(T)/SR
    x=np.zeros(T)
    for k,a in partials:
        x += a*np.sin(2*np.pi*F*k*t + k*phase_j)
    return x

def env_adsr(T, atk, dec, sus_lvl, rel, sus_end):
    e=np.ones(T)*sus_lvl
    a=int(min(T, atk*SR)); d=int(min(T-a, dec*SR)); r=int(min(T, rel*SR))
    if a>0: e[:a]=np.linspace(0,1,a)**1.5
    if d>0: e[a:a+d]=np.linspace(1,sus_lvl,d)
    s0=max(0, T-r)
    ramp=np.linspace(1,0,T-s0)**2
    e[s0:]*=ramp
    return e

def norm(x, amp=0.42):
    m=np.abs(x).max()
    return x/ (m if m>0 else 1) * amp

def as16(x): return (np.clip(x,-1,1)*32767).astype('<i2')

def lead(F):
    T=int(SR*0.9)
    p=[(k, 1/k**0.85) for k in range(1,34)] + [(k, 0.55/k**1.1) for k in range(1,20,2)]
    x=harm_wave(F,T,p)
    x+=0.18*harm_wave(F*1.0025,T,p)          # slight detune chorus (short, stays near-loopable)
    e=env_adsr(T,0.006,0.05,0.82,0.12,T)
    return as16(norm(x*e,0.40)), int(0.12*SR), T-int(0.14*SR)

def pad(F):
    T=int(SR*1.4)
    p=[(1,1.0),(2,0.34),(3,0.22),(4,0.13),(5,0.09),(6,0.05),(7,0.035),(8,0.02)]
    x=harm_wave(F,T,p,0.0)
    x+=0.5*harm_wave(F*0.9985,T,p,0.4)
    e=env_adsr(T,0.10,0.25,0.9,0.35,T)
    return as16(norm(x*e,0.34)), int(0.40*SR), T-int(0.40*SR)

def bassdrive(F):
    T=int(SR*0.42)
    p=[(k,1/k**0.55) for k in range(1,26)]+[(2,0.5),(4,0.25)]
    x=harm_wave(F,T,p)
    e=env_adsr(T,0.002,0.05,0.30,0.22,T)
    return as16(norm(x*e,0.46)), 0, 0     # one shot

def subbass(F):
    T=int(SR*0.9)
    x=harm_wave(F,T,[(1,1.0),(2,0.42),(3,0.16),(4,0.07)])
    e=env_adsr(T,0.004,0.08,0.55,0.25,T)
    return as16(norm(x*e,0.46)), int(0.2*SR), T-int(0.25*SR)

def pluck(F):
    T=int(SR*0.5)
    x=harm_wave(F,T,[(k,1/k**0.45) for k in range(1,40)])
    e=np.exp(-np.arange(T)/(SR*0.085))
    e[:20]=np.linspace(0,1,20)
    return as16(norm(x*e,0.44)), 0, 0

def kick(F):
    T=int(SR*0.30)
    t=np.arange(T)/SR
    f0=F*1.9
    fc=f0*np.exp(-t/0.035)+F*0.62
    ph=2*np.pi*np.cumsum(fc)/SR
    x=np.sin(ph)*np.exp(-t/0.11)
    click=np.random.RandomState(7).randn(T)*np.exp(-t/0.004)*0.35
    x=x+click
    # gentle lowpass on click
    return as16(norm(x,0.5)), 0, 0

def snare(F):
    T=int(SR*0.26)
    t=np.arange(T)/SR
    rs=np.random.RandomState(11)
    n=rs.randn(T)
    # bandpass-ish noise: difference of smoothed
    k=np.ones(6)/6
    nb=np.convolve(n,k,'same')
    tone=0.45*np.sin(2*np.pi*F*1.0*t)*np.exp(-t/0.045)+0.25*np.sin(2*np.pi*F*1.48*t)*np.exp(-t/0.03)
    x=(nb*0.9+tone)*np.exp(-t/0.07)
    x[:12]=np.linspace(0,1,12)*x[:12]
    return as16(norm(x,0.4)),0,0

def hat(F, open_=False):
    T=int(SR*(0.30 if open_ else 0.075))
    t=np.arange(T)/SR
    rs=np.random.RandomState(3 if open_ else 5)
    n=rs.randn(T)
    hp=n-np.convolve(n,np.ones(4)/4,'same')
    x=hp*np.exp(-t/(0.09 if open_ else 0.022))
    x[:8]=np.linspace(0,1,8)*x[:8]
    return as16(norm(x,0.30)),0,0

def swell():
    T=int(SR*1.6)
    t=np.arange(T)/SR
    rs=np.random.RandomState(9)
    n=rs.randn(T)
    band=np.convolve(n,np.ones(20)/20,'same')-np.convolve(n,np.ones(160)/160,'same')
    e=(t/T)**2.5*np.minimum(1,(1-t/T)*8)
    tone=0.3*np.sin(2*np.pi*(110+ 200*t/T)*t)
    x=(band*1.2+tone*e)*e
    return as16(norm(x,0.34)),0,0

29 minutes left. Simplify: drop arpeggio effects, drop volume-slide complexities. Focus on building the tune using: notes + volume column (dynamics), panning per instrument, multi-instrument timbres, and retriggered short samples. Everything sample-based.

Let me now write ONE build script that:
1. Generates 9 instruments with crafted 16-bit PCM samples (looped for sustains, one-shot for drums).
2. Creates a module via the MCP tool using sample_create_from_pcm (b64 <200KB per call — keep samples ≤8000 frames each to stay under the 240KB limit; b64 size = 16*N/... wait encoding int16: 2 bytes/sample → base64 ~ 2.67 bytes per sample. Limit 240KB per request → N ≤ ~85,000 samples. So 16-bit int16 PCM of up to ~85k samples OK (1.9s at 44.1k).

But loop_start/loop_length settable via sample_set.

3. Patterns via many pattern_set_cell calls → use `ft2 batch` with a JSON file for speed! batch executes a list of calls. That's the efficient way: one batch file with thousands of cell calls. The bridge sends one request at a time over the socket though (client-side loop) — each call has its own socket connect; ~10ms each → 10k calls = 100s. Acceptable but let me reduce: use rows 64 × 8 channels × ~20 patterns... I'll write only non-empty cells (typical ~30% density) → e.g. 20 patterns × 64 rows × 4 channels avg = 5,120 non-empty cells ≈ 1-2 min. OK.

Actually, faster: I could write the XM myself entirely (allowed: "Writing the XM bytes yourself is allowed") — but then it must be a real tracker module readable by FT2/ft2-clone (standard format). The risk: my writer must be perfect, and I can't verify since the fork can't load external XM... Let me test if the fork loads a standard XM quickly (that test failed on a bug; let me fix and test). If it loads and renders correctly, I can author the whole thing in standard XM bytes — that gives envelopes, all effects, and full control. But if my writer has a subtle bug, the trusted renderer might fail → catastrophic.

Given the fork's XM layout mismatch, the "trusted process renders the final XM" likely uses ft2-clone (the same binary!) which... hmm, ft2-clone the app reads standard XM. The fork's own save format is weird — but maybe the fork writes 9-byte headers and ALSO reads them (it round-tripped its own file fine). Real FT2/ft2-clone wouldn't read that properly...

Wait, actually maybe I misread the fork's layout. Let me reconsider: fork wrote `09 00 00 00 00 40 00 8a 00`. Standard FT2 writes pattern header length=9, packtype=0, nrows(2), nchan(2), patsize(2), then 2 reserved bytes. The fork's file has rows=64 at bytes 5-6 (`40 00`) and nchan at 7-8 (`8a 00` = 138) — this is wrong vs standard, but maybe it's just... hmm, standard FT2 writes: length(4)=9, packtype(1)=0, nrows(2), datasize(2), nchannels(2)!? No: nrows then datasize then nchannels? FT2 stores "Number of channels (WORD)" at offset 7 and "Pattern length (WORD)" at 5 and "Pattern data size" at 9. Hmm, that's what standard says: offset 5 = nrows, 7 = nchannels, 9 = patsize... but the fork wrote 138 at offset 7 (nchannels) and 0x013D=317 at offset 9 (patsize) — wait that's what I found: bytes at 336+5=341: `40 00` = 64 rows, at 343: `8a 00` = 138, at 345: `3d 01` = 317.

If offset 7 is nchannels=138 → wrong (song had 2 channels). If offset 7 held patsize... no, 317 is at offset 9.

Hold on! For a 2-channel, 64-row pattern: nrows=64 at offset 5 ✓, then offset 7 = 138... For a 2-channel pattern the patsize (uncompressed) = 64*(1+2*5)=704; compressed = 317. So offset 7 holds... 138?? Hmm 138 = 0x8A.

Oh! Maybe the fork writes pattern header as: length(4), packtype(1), nrows(2), nchannels(2), patsize(2) = 11 bytes header but declares length=9. So it writes 2 EXTRA bytes and declares 9. Then real layout = offset5 nrows=64, offset7 nchan... no wait if it wrote nchan at offset 7 we'd see 2, not 138.

Alternatively the fork writes: length(4)=9, packtype(1)=0, nrows(2)=64, patsize(2)=317, nchan(2)=2 → bytes would be 09 00 00 00 00 40 00 3d 01 02 00. But we saw 09 00 00 00 00 40 00 8a 00 3d 01. The 8a 00 (138) sits where patsize would be. 138 could be a bogus "nchannels" field computed from a bug... and then patsize 317 at offset 9.

Given nchannels at offset 7 is 138 (bogus) and header len declared 9 with data starting at offset 9 (after 11 header bytes?) — hmm, earlier the pattern data started at off+hlen = 345+... let me recheck: I found data starting at 336+9=345 = `3d 01` + `32 0a 05` ... hmm actually I found the first packed cell header 0x3D at 336+11=347.

Let me look at raw again: at 336: `09 00 00 00 | 00 | 40 00 | 8a 00 | 3d 01 | 32 0a 05 | 87 49 01 | 40 9c 50 | 41 08 ...`

Hmm! What if the actual header is 9 bytes (336..344): length=9, packtype=0, nrows=64, then `8a 00` = patsize?? 317 at offset 9 is at 345 — outside 9 bytes (336+9=345). So header = 9 bytes ending at 344, data starts at 345 = `3d 01 32 0a 05 87 49 ...`.

Wait, `3d 01` = 317 = patsize written at the END of the header (offset 7..8 within the 9-byte header, i.e., bytes 343-344)? Let me recount: 336:09,337:00,338:00,339:00,340:00,341:40,342:00,343:8a,344:00,345:3d,346:01,347:32. So a 9-byte header = 336..344: [length=9][packtype=0][nrows=64(2B)][8a 00]. That 8a 00 = 138 is nchannels?! But the song had 2 channels. Hmm, 138... 

And then at 345: `3d 01` = 317 = patsize, and data from 347.

So the fork writes an 11-byte header (length declared 9) where its own reader uses: length field(4) → skips 9 bytes → then reads patsize(2) → then reads packed data. So it reads patsize from offset 9, and nchannels from offset 7 = 138 (bogus, maybe an uninitialized value!).

Interesting: 138 = 0x8A. Hmm, in the round-trip test earlier, the file was loaded correctly (channels=2 preserved, pattern data preserved). So its reader ignores the nchannels field and uses the module's channel count. And the "pattern data" region is length 9 + patsize.

So the fork's format is: 11 bytes header, but "header length" declared = 9 → data starts at header+9, and 2 bytes of garbage (the declared patsize is at +7? no at +9).

Hmm: at +7: `8a 00` (garbage), at +9: `3d 01` (patsize). If data starts at +9, it overwrites... no: the reader reads 9 bytes header, then 2 bytes patsize, then data. That's consistent: header(9) + patsize(2) + data. Standard FT2: header length field = 9, and the 9 bytes = length(4)+packtype(1)+nrows(2)+patsize(2)!! YES! Standard XM pattern header is exactly: 4 bytes header length, 1 byte packtype, 2 bytes nrows, 2 bytes patsize = 9 bytes total, followed by data. nchannels is NOT in the standard pattern header! 

I misremembered the spec. Let me verify with the real XM spec:
```
Pattern header:
+0 WORD length of pattern header (9)
+4 BYTE pack type (0)
+5 WORD number of rows
+7 WORD packed data size  <-- wait...
+9 WORD number of channels
```
Hmm. The official XM spec:
```
Pattern header:
00 04 DWORD Size of pattern header (always 9)
04 01 BYTE Pack type (0 = zip type)
05 02 WORD Number of rows in pattern (1..256)
07 02 WORD Packed data size of pattern (uncompressed=rows*chan*5)  -- no...
```
Actually I recall: 
```
+5 2 rows
+7 2 datasize (packed)
+9 1 ??? 
```
Our fork's file has rows at +5=64, +7 = 0x8A=138, +9 = 0x013D=317 (packed size), +11 = data (0x32...).

If standard order is rows(+5), nchan(+7), patsize(+9) with header length 9 and data starting at +9 (overlapping the nchan/patsize fields)?? That can't be.

Whatever — the fork writes: length=9 declared, but data actually starts at 11 (347 in our example: `32 0a 05` = first packed cell with hdr 0x32 → note 0x3D=61 ✓). So the fork's reader skips 9+2 = 11 bytes? And the patsize it reads at +9=317 ✓ correct packed size.

So the fork layout = 4(len=9) + 1(pack) + 2(rows) + 2(??138) + 2(patsize) + data. The +7 field holds 138 — for a 2-channel pattern with 64 rows... 64*2*5=640 uncompressed; not 138. Maybe it's a bug where nchannels is written from an uninitialized buffer.

Given this mess, my safest path: submit a module SAVED BY THE FORK (guaranteed loadable by their pipeline) — i.e., build everything through MCP tools and call module_save. The trusted renderer presumably uses the same fork binary. Yes — "A trusted process renders the final XM separately" implies their pipeline reads what the fork writes. And the task says the workspace FT2 session save path is submission/tune.xm. So: build via tools, save via tools. That's the intended, safe route. Envelopes then must be baked into samples; effects limited to what actually works: porta/glissando (01/02/03/04), volume column + A/C slides, D note cut, E9 retrigger?, F tempo, B jump. Vibrato/tremolo don't work. Arpeggio doesn't work.

Wait, earlier tests showed 0x01/0x02 (porta) DO work, 0x0D (note cut) works (changed file length?! it truncated render... hmm cut D changed nf = truncation, suspicious), 0x0A vol slide works, 0x0C set vol works, 0x0F tempo works, 0x0B jump works, 0x0E sub-effects mostly no.

The "0x36..0x3F all produced nf=141120 vs base" — in that scan the base itself had f7a40d40/141120 and many eff changed... The scan output showed eff 0x00,0x01,0x02,0x05,0x06,0x08,0x0a,0x0b,0x0c,0x0d,0x0f,0x10,0x11,0x14,0x19,0x1b,0x1d changed. 0x0B/0x0D/0x0F changed nf (as expected for jump/cut/tempo). Note 0x00 (arpeggio) changed the audio (4 distinct hashes for different params) — so arpeggio DOES work! And 0x10? That's "pattern loop"? Hmm 0x10 with 4 params gave 4 different hashes — weird.

Earlier arpeggio tests at spd=6 suggested it cycles per row when placed with a note. Good enough — I'll test arpeggio quickly (it's great for bass/drone color) but I can live without it.

TIME PLAN (29 min):
1. Write build_all.py: sample generation + MCP calls via batch file + patterns + save + render + analysis. (~15 min to write, 5 min to run)
2. Inspect render, one revision pass.
3. Submit.

Simplify the arrangement to reduce risk: 8 channels, 64-row patterns, song of 16 orders, speed 6/bpm 168 → row 89.3ms; 64 rows = 5.71s per pattern.

Let me design concretely and compactly.

Key: A minor. Chords (root bass notes, MIDI):
- bar1: Am (A2=45) [Am add E], 
- bar2: F  (F2=41)
- bar3: G  (G2=43)
- bar4: E  (E2=40)
Phrase 2: Am, F, G, E again but melody variations.
Section B: Dm(38)? Let's do: C3=48? Use F(41), G(43), Am(45), Em(40)/C(36)...

Simpler: 4 chord loops used across sections: Am-F-G-E (section A), and for section B: F-G-Am-Am? and C(48)-G(43)-Am(45)-E(40)... I'll define progression per section explicitly in code with chord symbol → [root, third, fifth] MIDI lists. Let me use:
A: Am: [45, 52, 57, 60, 64], F: [41, 48, 53, 57, 60], G: [43, 50, 55, 59, 62], E: [40, 47, 52, 55, 59]
B (break): F: as above, G, Am, Em: [40,47,52,55,59]
C: C: [48, 55, 60, 64, 67], G, Am, E

Pads: 3 sustained chord tones per bar (one per channel), each bar = 16 rows.
Lead: 16th-based riff; I'll define per-bar note lists with (row, note, dur, vol).
Arp/bass-drive channel: repeated 8th-note root+fifth pulses on ch4 (fast decay pluck) — good "keygen" energy.
Kick ch5: pattern of quarters. Hat ch6: offbeats. Snare ch7: beats 2,4.

Per-pattern (64 rows = 4 bars).

Sections:
P0 Intro: drums+ kick/hat only + a rising filtered noise swell? Keep: bass root pulses + kick + hats + pad chord on Am (sustained) — a simple opening.
P1 A1: full: pad, lead riff A, bass pulses, drums.
P2 A2: same but variation lead + more hats.
P3 B (break): pads + arp + soft kick.
P4 A3 (=P1) 
P5 A4 (lead variation, higher octave)
P6 C (climax, new lead in C major-ish? keep Am), full volumes.
P7 Outro: pads fade + topline, ends on Am with long decay.
Then loop back to P0 — intro is minimal so the loop point feels like a natural "restart"; the last pattern should decay into it. To make the loop clean, keep the final pattern ending with the pad releasing and a short noise fill, then P0 begins with the downbeat kick.

Total 8 patterns × 5.71s = 45.7s.

Now sample set (each ≤ ~2s, mono 16-bit, mostly looped):
- inst 0 unused
- 1: "Lead" bright saw+square hybrid with fast attack, slight decay to 80%, looped. 
- 2: "Pad" soft warm (sine+triangle stack, chorus via detune), slow attack, looped.
- 3: "BassDrive" short punchy saw, decays in 0.2s (one shot, no loop) for 8th pulses.
- 4: "Pluck/Arp" karplus-strong-ish? Use a bright pluck with 0.35s decay, no loop.
- 5: "SubBass" sine+10% even harmonics, decay 0.25, no loop (kick-bass combo) — actually use for long bass notes (looped).
- 6: "Kick" pitch-swept sine with click, no loop, 0.28s.
- 7: "Snare" noise+tonal, 0.22s, no loop.
- 8: "Hat" filtered noise 0.06s (closed) and open: two samples in one instrument mapped by key (relative/keymap!). Keymap: I can map different notes to different samples within one instrument! keymap array 96 bytes maps note→sample index. YES: instrument 8: sample0=closed hat (note 57=C#5?), sample1=open hat (note 61). Need to double check the fork's renderer respects keymap... Earlier relative_note=57 broke things (silence for notes above). Risky. Let me test keymap quickly: 2 samples in an instrument with keymap mapping; render notes.

Given time, safer: separate instruments (9 total): 1 Lead, 2 Pad, 3 Bass, 4 Pluck, 5 SubBass(looped low), 6 Kick, 7 Snare, 8 HatC, 9 HatO. Fine (instrument count is arbitrary).

Panning per instrument: Lead 108, Pad 96/160 → need two pad instruments for stereo width? Pad: inst 2 pan 100 and inst 10 "PadR" pan 156? Simpler: use the same sample data for a second pad instrument with different panning (extra memory, small). I'll do: 2=PadL(pan 88), 11=PadR(pan 168) sharing sample bytes but separate instruments (each sample_create_from_pcm call again). Memory fine.

Arpeggio: maybe use inst 4 Pluck for chord tones at fast rate.

OK. Sample data length: keep each ≤ 1.0s (44100 samples = 88KB raw → b64 117KB, fits 240KB limit). Pad needs 2s attack? Pad loop at 1s with 0.3s attack is fine.

Sample pitch: bake so root note = C-5 (note 61 = 49+12) plays at the sample's fundamental. I'll generate each sample at the frequency of its lowest needed note and pitch UP as needed (upsampling pitch raises pitch = good, avoids sub-nyquist issues; downsampling too far is fine as long as content isn't above nyquist/2). To be safe: generate samples at the frequency of the LOWEST note used for that instrument, set relative_note=61, and use notes ≥ lowest.

Frequencies: A1 lead range 69..81 → generate lead at note 69 = A4 440Hz ✓.
Pad: notes ~52..67 → generate at 52 (E3=164.81).
Bass: notes 40..45 → generate at 40 (E2=82.41). Low sample rate content — fine.
Pluck: 57..72 → generate 57 (A3 220).
Subbass: 40..45 → 40.
Kick: fundamental sweep 120→45; use note 45 (A2=110) as base... I'll bake at 55 for lowest note 40? Simpler: kick tuned so note 48 = ~100Hz thump; use notes 45-50 → generate accordingly (bake the sweep starting from f_note*2 → 50Hz).
Snare: tonal ~180 + noise → base note 57.
Hats: noise, no pitch need; but pitch changes with note — bake at the exact note I'll use: hat closed note 73, open note 72. Keep amplitude low so higher/lower notes rarely used.

Now let me write the generator functions carefully (compact, no heavy computation).

Lead waveform: saw with 24 harmonics (1/11 decay) + square-ish (odd harmonics 1/k) mix, slight vibrato baked? No vibrato — but a slow amplitude "chorus" via two detuned copies (±0.4%) baked into the loop → gives movement. Loops: need loop_start/loop_length; baked chorus means the loop should be long (whole 1s as loop, seamless if the waveform is periodic... detuned sum isn't periodic at 1s. Better: keep lead a pure harmonic stack (periodic at fundamental period) and loop exactly one period? At 440Hz one period = 100 samples → loop 1 period = perfectly seamless sustain. Then shaping comes from... nothing (sustain forever, no articulation). Hmm — but I have note cuts (D) and volume slides, and note retriggers give "articulation" only via the sample's attack which the loop skips.

Compromise: bake an amplitude envelope that reaches a steady value and loop the steady part (as computed earlier). Lead: attack 8ms → decay 60ms to 0.8 → loop steady region. Loops of ~44100 samples (1s) each with the loop region starting at 0.1s. With 6-12 notes in flight, ~0.2-0.35 amplitude per voice.

I'll use a "loop-and-fade" trick: because loops sustain forever, a held note will ring indefinitely unless cut. For the Pad, that's fine (pads are meant to sustain). For the Lead, sustaining is also fine — classic chiptune leads sustain. For bass pulses, use one-shots (no loop) so they decay naturally.

That's actually a clean design: sustained timbres (lead, pad) loop; percussive timbres (bass, pluck, drums) are one-shots that decay.

Great. Now write everything in one script. Let me be efficient and careful.

Volume levels: sample volume 64 max. Note volumes: use 64 for forte, 48 mf, 40 mp, 32 p, 24 pp.

Let me write it now — code first, then run, then examine.

Also: `song_set({'global_volume':...})` maybe. Keep 64.

Patterns: to limit calls, I'll only write non-empty cells.

Effects I'll use: 0x0F (tempo) for a breakdown slowdown? risky; skip. 0x0D note cut at end of last pattern for clean release. 0x0A volume slide for the final fade-out. Use 0x02 porta on the lead for a few slides (nice touch). Keep it minimal to avoid surprises — but porta is verified working, and volume slides work.

One more consideration: the loop. The song restarts at order 0. I'll set loop_start=0. The last pattern should end with everything released (note-offs/cuts) so the restart is clean, and the intro starts with a strong downbeat.

Let me write the code.

import numpy as np
SR=44100
def f_of_note(n): return 440.0*2**((n-69)/12)

def harm_wave(F, T, partials, phase_j=0.13):
    """partials: list of (harmonic_index, amplitude)"""

    x=np.zeros(T)
    for k,a in partials:

    return x

    e=np.ones(T)*sus_lvl
    a=int(min(T, atk*SR)); d=int(min(T-a, dec*SR)); r=int(min(T, rel*SR))

    if d>0: e[a:a+d]=np.linspace(1,sus_lvl,d)
    s0=max(0, T-r)
    ramp=np.linspace(1,0,T-s0)**2
    e[s0:]*=ramp
    return e

def norm(x, amp=0.42):
    m=np.abs(x).max()

def as16(x): return (np.clip(x,-1,1)*32767).astype('<i2')

    e=env_adsr(T,0.10,0.25,0.9,0.35,T)
    return as16(norm(x*e,0.34)), int(0.40*SR), T-int(0.40*SR)

    T=int(SR*0.42)
    p=[(k,1/k**0.55) for k in range(1,26)]+[(2,0.5),(4,0.25)]

    e=env_adsr(T,0.002,0.05,0.30,0.22,T)

    x=harm_wave(F,T,[(1,1.0),(2,0.42),(3,0.16),(4,0.07)])
    e=env_adsr(T,0.004,0.08,0.55,0.25,T)
    return as16(norm(x*e,0.46)), int(0.2*SR), T-int(0.25*SR)

def pluck(F):
    T=int(SR*0.5)
    x=harm_wave(F,T,[(k,1/k**0.45) for k in range(1,40)])
    e=np.exp(-np.arange(T)/(SR*0.085))
    e[:20]=np.linspace(0,1,20)
    return as16(norm(x*e,0.44)), 0, 0

def kick(F):
    T=int(SR*0.30)
    t=np.arange(T)/SR
    f0=F*1.9
    fc=f0*np.exp(-t/0.035)+F*0.62
    ph=2*np.pi*np.cumsum(fc)/SR

    return as16(norm(x,0.5)), 0, 0

def snare(F):
    T=int(SR*0.26)

    rs=np.random.RandomState(11)

    k=np.ones(6)/6
    nb=np.convolve(n,k,'same')
    tone=0.45*np.sin(2*np.pi*F*1.0*t)*np.exp(-t/0.045)+0.25*np.sin(2*np.pi*F*1.48*t)*np.exp(-t/0.03)
    x=(nb*0.9+tone)*np.exp(-t/0.07)
    x[:12]=np.linspace(0,1,12)*x[:12]
    return as16(norm(x,0.4)),0,0

def hat(F, open_=False):

    x=hp*np.exp(-t/(0.09 if open_ else 0.022))
    x[:8]=np.linspace(0,1,8)*x[:8]
    return as16(norm(x,0.30)),0,0

def swell():
    T=int(SR*1.6)

    band=np.convolve(n,np.ones(20)/20,'same')-np.convolve(n,np.ones(160)/160,'same')
    e=(t/T)**2.5*np.minimum(1,(1-t/T)*8)
    tone=0.3*np.sin(2*np.pi*(110+ 200*t/T)*t)
    x=(band*1.2+tone*e)*e
    return as16(norm(x,0.34)),0,0

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/workspace/work')
from xmstd import *
from f2 import call
import numpy as np, wave
SR=44100
d=np.sin(2*np.pi*440*np.arange(int(SR*0.8))/SR)*0.45
s=Sample('lead', (d*32767).astype('<i2'), loop_start=2000, loop_length=20000, volume=64, panning=100, relative=57, c4spd=8363)
inst=Instrument('STDTEST',[s], venv=Env(pts=[(0,0),(16,64),(120,50),(400,0)]))

for r in range(32):

    if r==24: row[1]=(97,0,0,0,0)
    rows.append(row)
xm=build('STANDARDXM',[0],[rows],[inst],nchannels=2,speed=6,bpm=150)
open('/workspace/work/std.xm','wb').write(xm)
print('bytes',len(xm))
print('load:',call('module_load',{'path':'/workspace/work/std.xm'}))
print('info:',call('module_info',{})[0])

def V(amp):
    v=int(round(16+48*(amp/64.0)))
    return max(17,min(76,v))
def C(note,ins,amp,eff=0,par=0): return (note,ins,V(amp),eff,par)
OFF=(97,0,0,0,0); EMPTY=(0,0,0,0,0)
def grid(edits):
    g=[[EMPTY]*NCH for _ in range(ROWS)]
    for (r,c),cell in edits.items():
        if 0<=r<ROWS: g[r][c]=cell
    return g

CM = dict(pad=[52,55,60,64], bass=28, arp=[55,60,64,67])
GM = dict(pad=[55,59,62,67], bass=31, arp=[59,62,67,71])
EM = dict(pad=[56,59,64,68], bass=28, arp=[56,59,64,68])
DM = dict(pad=[50,53,57,62], bass=26, arp=[50,57,62,65])
PROG1=[AM,FM,CM,GM]
PROG2=[DM,AM,EM,GM]

def drumset(kick16, snare16, hat16, extra=None):
    """returns list of (row, channel, note, ins, amp) with row = bar*16+i"""
    out=[]
    for i in kick16: out.append((i,5,61,7,64))
    for i in snare16: out.append((i,6,61,8,58))
    for i,a in hat16: out.append((i,7,73,9,a))
    if extra: out.extend(extra)
    return out
K_A=[0,6,8,14]; S_A=[4,12]; H_A=[(i,26) for i in range(0,16,2)]
K_A2=[0,3,8,10]; S_A2=[4,12,15]; H_A2=[(0,26),(2,22),(4,26),(6,22),(8,26),(10,22),(12,26),(14,22),(15,18)]
K_B=[0,8,11]; S_B=[4,12]; H_B=[(i,24) for i in range(16)]
K_BREAK=[0]; S_BREAK=[]; 
# ---------- pattern builders ----------
def mk_lead(mel):
    e={}
    for (r,n,l,a) in mel:
        e[(r,0)]=C(n,1,a)
        if r+l<ROWS: e[(r+l,0)]=OFF
    return e
def mk_pad(prog, amps=(38,32,30,26), octave=12):
    e={}
    for bar in range(4):
        ch=prog[bar]['pad']
        for i,nt in enumerate(ch):
            e[(bar*16, 2 if i<2 else 3)]=C(nt+octave,4 if False else 4, amps[i])
            if bar*16+15<ROWS: e[(bar*16+15, 2 if i<2 else 3)]=OFF
    return e

    """pat: list of (row_in_bar, semitone_offset_or_None, amp, dur)"""
    e={}

        for (r,off,a,dur) in pat:
            row=bar*16+r
            if off is None: continue
            e[(row,4)]=C(rt+off,ins,a)
            if row+dur<ROWS: e[(row+dur,4)]=OFF

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/workspace/work')
from f2 import call
import numpy as np, wave
SR=44100
def one(rel=None, note=61, vol=64, sv=64, pan=128, loop=None, samp='lead', amp=16):
    call('module_new',{'channels':1,'name':'dg'})
    call('sample_load',{'path':f'/workspace/work/samples/{samp}.wav','instrument':1,'sample':0})
    a={'instrument':1,'sample':0,'volume':sv,'panning':pan}
    if rel is not None: a['relative_note']=rel
    if loop: a.update(loop_start=loop[0],loop_length=loop[1],flags=1)
    call('sample_set',a)
    call('pattern_set_length',{'pattern':0,'rows':16})
    call('song_set',{'bpm':150,'speed':6,'length':1})
    call('pattern_set_cell',{'pattern':0,'row':0,'channel':0,'note':note,'instrument':1,'volume':vol})
    call('module_render',{'path':'/workspace/work/dg.wav','rate':SR,'bits':16,'amp':amp})
    ww=wave.open('work/dg.wav'); d=np.frombuffer(ww.readframes(ww.getnframes()),dtype='<i2').astype(float)/32768
    st=d.reshape(-1,2); x=st[:,0]+st[:,1]
    seg=x[int(3*4410):int(9*4410)]
    from numpy.fft import rfft,rfftfreq
    N=len(seg); sp=np.abs(rfft(seg*np.hanning(N))); fr=rfftfreq(N,1/SR)
    i=int(np.argmax(sp))
    return 12*np.log2(fr[i]/587.33) if fr[i]>1 else float('nan'), float(np.abs(x).max()), float(np.sqrt((seg**2).mean()))
print('no rel set     ', one())
print('rel=61         ', one(rel=61))
print('rel=49         ', one(rel=49))
print('rel=57         ', one(rel=57))
print('rel=61 loop    ', one(rel=61, loop=(13230,7350)))
print('no rel  loop   ', one(loop=(13230,7350)))
print('note57 norel   ', one(note=57))
print('note69 norel   ', one(note=69))
print('amp32          ', one(amp=32))
print('sv=32          ', one(sv=32))
EOF
python3 work/diag.py

import numpy as np, wave, os
SR=44100; REF=261.63    # content frequency == XM note 61 (C-5) in this fork
def to16(x, amp):
    x=np.asarray(x,float); x=x-x.mean(); m=np.abs(x).max()
    if m>0: x=x/m*amp
    return (np.clip(x,-1,1)*32767).astype('<i2')
def wave_add(F, secs, spec, vib=None, det=0.0, phase=0.13):
    n=int(SR*secs); t=np.arange(n)/SR
    if vib is None:
        ph=2*np.pi*F*(1+det)*t
    else:
        rate,depth = vib
        env=np.minimum(1.0,t/0.25)
        inst=1.0+depth*np.sin(2*np.pi*rate*t)*env+det
        ph=2*np.pi*F*np.cumsum(inst)/SR
    x=np.zeros(n); km=int(18500/max(F,1))
    for k,a in spec:
        if 0<k<=km: x+=a*np.sin(k*ph+phase*k)
    return x,t,n
def shaped(n, a, d, s, r):
    e=np.ones(n)*s
    A=int(n*a); D=int(n*d); R=min(int(n*r), n-1)
    if A>0: e[:A]=np.linspace(0,1,A)**1.2
    if D>0: e[A:A+D]=np.linspace(1,s,D)
    if R>0: e[n-R:]*=np.linspace(1,0,R)**1.5
    return e
def lead():
    spec=[(k,1.0/k**0.85) for k in range(1,22)]+[(2,0.30),(4,0.16)]
    x,t,n=wave_add(REF,0.95,spec,vib=(6.0,0.0055))
    y,_,_=wave_add(REF*1.0016,0.95,spec[:12],vib=(6.0,0.0075))
    x=x+0.45*y
    e=shaped(n,0.003,0.05,0.78,0.28)
    per=int(round(SR/6.0))                     # 7350 samples = one vibrato period
    ls=per*2; ll=per
    return to16(x*e,0.40), ls, ll
def pad():
    spec=[(1,1.0),(2,0.34),(3,0.26),(4,0.17),(5,0.11),(6,0.07),(7,0.05),(8,0.035),(9,0.025),(10,0.018)]
    n=int(SR*1.6); acc=np.zeros(n)
    for j,(det,am) in enumerate([(0.000,1.0),(0.0045,0.8),(-0.0055,0.7),(0.0095,0.5)]):
        y,t,_=wave_add(REF*(1+det),1.6,spec,vib=(0.8+0.1*j,0.0038))
        acc+=am*y
    t=np.arange(n)/SR
    e=np.minimum(1,t/0.3)*np.minimum(1,np.maximum(0,(1.6-t)/0.3))
    ls=int(0.35*SR); ll=int(1.0*SR)            # exactly 1 second loop (integer periods for 261.63-ish not needed: crossfade-free but long)
    return to16(acc*e,0.30), ls, ll
def bass():
    spec=[(k,1.0/k**0.55) for k in range(1,12)]+[(2,0.5),(4,0.28)]

    return to16(x*shaped(n,0.0015,0.05,0.30,0.14),0.48),0,0
def sub():
    spec=[(1,1.0),(2,0.5),(3,0.2),(4,0.1),(5,0.05)]
    x,t,n=wave_add(REF,0.55,spec)
    return to16(x*shaped(n,0.006,0.06,0.6,0.22),0.48),0,0
def pluck():
    spec=[(k,1.0/k**0.5) for k in range(1,20)]

def pluck2():
    spec=[(k,(1.0 if k%2 else 0.4)/k**0.62) for k in range(1,16)]

    e=np.exp(-t/0.075); e[:10]=np.linspace(0,1,10)
    return to16(x*e,0.42),0,0
def kick(F=105.0):
    n=int(SR*0.33); t=np.arange(n)/SR
    fc=F*3.0*np.exp(-t/0.028)+F*0.9

    rs=np.random.RandomState(7)
    x=x*0.95+rs.randn(n)*np.exp(-t/0.0032)*0.18
    return to16(x,0.50),0,0
def snare(F=196.0):
    n=int(SR*0.28); t=np.arange(n)/SR
    rs=np.random.RandomState(11); nz=rs.randn(n)

    n=int(SR*2.2); t=np.arange(n)/SR

    n=int(SR*0.35); t=np.arange(n)/SR
    fc=F*1.8*np.exp(-t/0.08)+F*0.8
    x=np.sin(2*np.pi*np.cumsum(fc)/SR)*np.exp(-t/0.12)

    return to16(x,0.42),0,0

{"command": "cd /workspace && cat > work/dcheck.py <<'EOF'
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/workspace/work')
from f2 import call
import numpy as np, wave
from numpy.fft import rfft,rfftfreq
SR=44100
def one(samp, note, vol=64, win=(0.01,0.35)):
    call('module_new',{'channels':1,'name':'dc'})
    call('sample_load',{'path':f'/workspace/work/samples/{samp}.wav','instrument':1,'sample':0})
    call('sample_set',{'instrument':1,'sample':0,'volume':64,'panning':128})
    call('pattern_set_length',{'pattern':0,'rows':48})
    call('song_set',{'bpm':150,'speed':6,'length':1})
    call('pattern_set_cell',{'pattern':0,'row':0,'channel':0,'note':note,'instrument':1,'volume':vol})
    call('module_render',{'path':'/workspace/work/dc.wav','rate':SR,'bits':16,'amp':32})
    ww=wave.open('work/dc.wav'); d=np.frombuffer(ww.readframes(ww.getnframes()),dtype='<i2').astype(float)/32768
    x=d.reshape(-1,2)[:,0]+d.reshape(-1,2)[:,1]
    k=int(44100*2.5/150/6)  # one row
    seg=x[int(win[0]*SR):min(int(win[1]*SR),int(k*2))]
    N=len(seg); sp=np.abs(rfft(seg*np.hanning(N))); fr=rfftfreq(N,1/SR); i=int(np.argmax(sp))
    return round(float(fr[i]),1), round(float(np.abs(x).max()),3)
for s,n in [('kick',37),('kick',49),('kick',61),('snare',45),('snare',57),('tom',45),('tom',57),('bass',33),('bass',45),('sub',33),('hat',73),('pluck',73),('pluck2',61),('swell',61)]:
    print(f'{s:7s} n{n}', one(s,n))
EOF
python3 work/dcheck.py"}

messages.reasoning_content:
Good: everything is 2 octaves above what I assumed for drums (kick at note 37 = 105 Hz ✓ correct because my kick content was 105 at REF... wait kick content F=105 was synthesized at absolute 105 Hz and plays at 105 Hz for note 37?? Since sample "content frequency" corresponds to note 61, playing note 37 (24 semitones lower) should give 105/4 = 26 Hz. But measured 105.3 Hz at note 37. Hmm, that means kick content was 421 Hz (fc sweep from F*3.0 with F=105 → 315 initial...). Actually the dominant measured freq is the fundamental after the sweep: F*0.9 = 94.5... 

Let me reconsider: for the kick with F=105, the sine at end settles to ~94.5 Hz. Measured at note 37 → 105.3. And at note 49 → 136.8, at note 61 → 200. Ratios: 200/136.8 = 1.46 ≈ 2^(5.7/12)... hmm not exactly 2. And 136.8/105.3=1.30. Odd. Probably the pitch is dominated by different parts of the transient decay. Never mind — drums don't need exact pitch. What matters: kick gets lower with lower note. So for kick, use note 61 as "default" mapping where content = measured 200 Hz... I synthesized with F=105 meaning fundamental ~94.5 settling. Measured at note61 = 200 = 2× ~94.5 (harmonic emphasis?) fine.

Key mapping conclusion: sample content frequency C(n) plays at C(n)*2^((note-61)/12)? Let me verify with bass: content 261.63*? bass spec fundamental = REF=261.63. Measured at note 45 = 210.5?? Hmm, no. bass at note 45 measured 421, at note 33 measured 210.5. So ratio: 45-33=12 semitones → 210.5*2=421 ✓. And content 261.63 → at note 49 it should be 261.63. Given note 45 → 221 (261.63*2^(-4/12)=207). Measured 210.5 at note 33 → note 45 = 421? Wait the mapping says note 61 = content. So note 45 = content * 2^-16/12 = 261.63*0.397=103.8. But measured 421! That's 4× too high... 421/103.8 = 4.05. So actual: content pitch corresponds to note 61+24=85?? Hmm, earlier lead tests: lead n61 → measured dominant 0.2 semis off using want=261.63*2^((note-61)/12) ✓ (lead is harmonic-rich so fundamental identified). For the bass (short one-shot), my analysis window 0.005-0.10s captures the click transient with strong high harmonics, so peak is a harmonic. 421 = 2× 210.5, consistent with a harmonic too.

Anyway: the important checks (lead, pad) confirm note 61 = content 261.63, and relative_note default 49 means... wait, my diag showed 'no rel set' → +12 semitones above want-computation for content 261.63 at note 61? Earlier diag used lead.wav content 587 (old) so unclear. The new qcheck used want=261.63*2^((note-61)/12) and lead measured +0.2 semis at notes 61, 69, 81. So default (no relative_note set) → note 61 = content. 

So: do NOT set relative_note at all (leave the fork's default which apparently equals 49... whatever it is, it behaves as "note 61 plays content frequency"). Hmm but wait: sample_load may set relative_note=49 internally, and 49 in the fork's naming = C-4 = MIDI C5... and the fork's note 61 = "C-5" = 2× C-4. Then playing note 61 with rel 49 should give 2× content, i.e. +12 semis. But measured +0.2. So the fork's internal sample->note mapping treats the stored relative as C-5-equivalent. Fine — empirically: leave it alone and note 61 = content.

But careful: sample_load might reset relative_note each time, and my qcheck didn't set it → +0.2 ✓. In the tune.py I set relative_note=61 → silence (bad). So remove that.

Now let me fix the composition: 
1. Don't set relative_note.
2. Set loop flags only for lead/pad with correct loop points (lead 14700,7350; pad 15435,44100).
3. Raise volumes: peak was 0.12 with amp=16. I'll use amp default and V() mapping to keep amplitudes sane. Also global_volume=64 default. Use render amp=24 maybe. For the submission, the trusted process renders separately with unknown amp; better make the tune peak near full scale with default amp... Unknown. I'll target internal peaks so at amp=16 (mid) we're around 0.5-0.8. Currently 0.12 at amp=16 → need ~4-5× more. My V() mapping compressed everything (16+48*amp/64 with amp≤64 → v between 16 and 64... that's right). The low output is because I used default volume per instrument (58 etc.) * note vol ~ small. Hmm: note volume V(58)=16+48*58/64=59.5 → 59; sample volume 58; combined = 59/64*58/64 = 0.84 relative... that's fine. But measured peak 0.12 vs a single lead note at full (64,64) → 0.716 at amp=32 → 0.36 at amp=16. So mix peak 0.12 means many channels are quiet/silent? Let me check per-section RMS to see which patterns are silent. Actually the RMS trace showed sections with 0.006-0.008 — very quiet overall. Something's off: maybe my pad edits overwrite each other (I had a bug: `e[(bar*16, 2 if i<2 else 3)]` merges - only last wins, so 1 pad note per bar). And bass/arp notes may be fine but the melody OFF events at r+l may clobber notes.

The real problem could be that with song length 8 patterns × 64 rows at 150bpm/6 = 51.2s ✓ matches. RMS 0.009 overall is low but the max was 0.041 in the drop.

Let me be efficient: rewrite the composition cleanly with a compact arrangement language, then check the mix by RMS per section and spectral content. Also increase volumes.

Also for a good keygen sound I want the arp/lead to be prominent. Let me write the final tune script carefully in one go, and verify.

Plan per channel (8):
ch0 LEAD (melody)
ch1 PLUCK-A (arp 16ths)
ch2 PAD (notes 1-2)
ch3 PAD (notes 3-4)
ch4 BASS (drive one-shot)
ch5 KICK
ch6 SNARE/TOM
ch7 HAT/HATO/SWELL

Patterns (64 rows each, 4 bars of 16):
P0 intro: pad + swell + sparse melody
P1 A1: melody MEL1, bass BASS1, arp, drums K_A
P2 A2: melody MEL2, drums busier
P3 B: different prog, melody solo
P4 drop: MEL3, driving bass 16ths, full drums
P5 A1 repeat w/ variation
P6 outro: fade with arps + pad

Order: 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,0? Loop back to position 1 (restart=1). Set loop_start=1 so intro plays once.

import wave, numpy as np
from numpy.fft import rfft,rfftfreq
SR=44100

st=d.reshape(-1,2)
rowlen=SR*6*2.5/150
# rms per pattern (64 rows = 12.8 s)
for p in range(8):
    seg=st[int(p*64*rowlen):int((p+1)*64*rowlen)]

# spectrum of slot 2 (index 2) lead region
def spec(a,b):
    x=st[int(a*rowlen):int(b*rowlen)]
    m=(x[:,0]+x[:,1])/2
    N=len(m); sp=np.abs(rfft(m*np.hanning(N))); fr=rfftfreq(N,1/SR)
    top=np.argsort(sp)[-10:][::-1]
    return [(round(float(fr[i]),1),round(float(sp[i]/sp.max()),2)) for i in sorted(top)]
print('slot1 rows0-16', spec(64,64+16))
print('slot1 rows48-64', spec(64+48,128))

{"command": "cd /workspace && python3 - <<'EOF'
import wave, numpy as np
from numpy.fft import rfft,rfftfreq
SR=44100
w=wave.open('work/tune2.wav'); nf=w.getnframes(); d=np.frombuffer(w.readframes(nf),dtype='<i2').astype(float)/32768
st=d.reshape(-1,2)
L=st[:,0]; R=st[:,1]
print('DC L/R', round(float(L.mean()),5), round(float(R.mean()),5))
rowlen=SR*6*2.5/150
def notes_in(a,b,fmax=8000):
    x=(L[a*rowlen:b*rowlen]+R[a*rowlen:b*rowlen])/2
    N=len(x); sp=np.abs(rfft(x*np.hanning(N))); fr=rfftfreq(N,1/SR)
    pk=[]
    for i in range(2,len(sp)-2):
        if sp[i]>sp[i-1] and sp[i]>sp[i+1] and sp[i]>0.10*sp.max() and fr[i]<fmax:
            pk.append((round(float(fr[i]),1),round(float(sp[i]/sp.max()),2)))
    # match to nearest semitone of 261.63 reference
    names=[]
    for f,m in pk:
        n=61+12*np.log2(f/261.63)
        names.append((round(float(n),2),m))
    return names[:14]
print('intro rows2-16:', notes_in(2,16,3000))
print('sec1 bar1 rows1-3:', notes_in(65,68,1200))
print('sec1 last bar:', notes_in(128+48,128+63,1200))
# check clicks: sample-to-sample jumps
diff=np.abs(np.diff(st,axis=0))
big=np.where(diff.max(axis=1)>0.30)[0]
print('possible clicks at frames', big[:20], 'count', len(big))
EOF"}

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/workspace/work')
from f2 import call
import wave, numpy as np
from numpy.fft import rfft,rfftfreq
SR=44100
def one(samp, note, loop=None, rows=48, win=(1.0,2.2)):
    call('module_new',{'channels':1,'name':'qc2'})
    call('sample_load',{'path':f'/workspace/work/samples/{samp}.wav','instrument':1,'sample':0})
    a={'instrument':1,'sample':0,'volume':64,'panning':128}
    if loop: a.update(loop_start=loop[0],loop_length=loop[1],flags=1)
    call('sample_set',a)
    call('pattern_set_length',{'pattern':0,'rows':rows})
    call('song_set',{'bpm':150,'speed':6,'length':1})
    call('pattern_set_cell',{'pattern':0,'row':0,'channel':0,'note':note,'instrument':1,'volume':64})
    call('module_render',{'path':'/workspace/work/qc2.wav','rate':SR,'bits':16,'amp':32})
    ww=wave.open('work/qc2.wav'); d=np.frombuffer(ww.readframes(ww.getnframes()),dtype='<i2').astype(float)/32768
    x=d.reshape(-1,2)[:,0]+d.reshape(-1,2)[:,1]
    seg=x[int(win[0]*SR):int(win[1]*SR)]
    N=len(seg); sp=np.abs(rfft(seg*np.hanning(N))); fr=rfftfreq(N,1/SR); i=int(np.argmax(sp))
    want=261.63*2**((note-61)/12)
    return round(float(fr[i]),1), round(float(want),1), round(12*np.log2(fr[i]/want),1) if fr[i]>4 else 'nan'
for n in [33,39,45,46,49,50,53,57,61,65,73]:

print()
for n in [33,39,45,49,57,61,73]:

s=open('work/tune2.py').read()

s=s.replace("(13,7,73,10,22)","(13,7,73,10,34)")

s=s.replace("(2,6,69,12,26),(10,6,73,12,24)","(2,6,69,12,32),(10,6,73,12,28)")
s=s.replace("(15,6,69,12,24)","(15,6,69,12,30)")
s=s.replace("(14,6,61,8,40)","(14,6,61,8,44)")

EOF
python3 work/tune2.py 2>&1|tail -2 && python3 - <<'EOF'
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/workspace/work')
from f2 import call
import wave, numpy as np
call('module_load',{'path':'/workspace/submission/tune.xm'})
print(call('module_render',{'path':'/workspace/work/hot.wav','rate':44100,'bits':16,'amp':32})[0])
w=wave.open('work/hot.wav'); nf=w.getnframes(); d=np.frombuffer(w.readframes(nf),dtype='<i2').astype(float)/32768
print('peak',round(float(np.abs(d).max()),3),'clipped samples',int(np.sum(np.abs(d)>=0.999)))
st=d.reshape(-1,2)
row=44100*6*2.5/150
# check bass band energy per section
for name,a,b in [('intro',0,64),('A1',64,128),('A2',128,192),('brk',192,256),('drop',256,320),('B',320,384),('A3',384,448)]:
    seg=st[int(a*row):int(b*row)]
    x=(seg[:,0]+seg[:,1])/2
    from numpy.fft import rfft,rfftfreq
    N=len(x); sp=np.abs(rfft(x*np.hanning(N))); fr=rfftfreq(N,1/44100)
    def band(lo,hi): 
        m=(fr>=lo)&(fr<hi); return round(float(np.sqrt((sp[m]**2).sum())/np.sqrt((sp**2).sum())*100),1)
    print(f'{name:6s} low<120:{band(20,120):5} mid:{band(120,800):5} hi:{band(800,3000):5} air:{band(3000,12000):5}')
EOF

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/workspace/work')
from f2 import call
import wave, numpy as np
from numpy.fft import rfft,rfftfreq
SR=44100
call('module_load',{'path':'/workspace/submission/tune.xm'})
print(call('module_info',{})[0])
call('module_render',{'path':'/workspace/work/final.wav','rate':SR,'bits':16,'amp':16})
w=wave.open('work/final.wav'); nf=w.getnframes(); d=np.frombuffer(w.readframes(nf),dtype='<i2').astype(float)/32768
st=d.reshape(-1,2); x=(st[:,0]+st[:,1])/2
row=int(SR*6*2.5/150)
def peaks(a,b,lo=100,hi=1400):
    s=x[int(a*row):int(b*row)]
    N=len(s); sp=np.abs(rfft(s*np.hanning(N))); fr=rfftfreq(N,1/SR)
    out=[]
    for i in range(1,len(sp)-1):
        if fr[i]>lo and fr[i]<hi and sp[i]>sp[i-1] and sp[i]>=sp[i+1] and sp[i]>0.12*sp.max():
            n=61+12*np.log2(fr[i]/261.63)
            out.append(round(float(n),2))
    return out[:12]
print('sec1 bar1 melody+bass peaks:',peaks(65,69))
print('intro bar2:',peaks(2,6))
# loop seam continuity: compare energy of last 2 rows vs first 2 rows of pattern0 slot
e_last=float(np.sqrt((x[-int(2*row):]**2).mean())); e_first=float(np.sqrt((x[:int(2*row)]**2).mean()))
print('rms last2rows',round(e_last,4),' first2rows',round(e_first,4))
print('dur',round(nf/SR,2),'s  peak',round(float(np.abs(d).max()),3))
EOF

The module is complete and verified. Final summary of what I built:

**"NEON CHAPEL"** — an original 8-channel keygen tune in the FastTracker II tracker tradition.

**Sound design** (all synthesized from scratch in NumPy, loaded as 16-bit samples):
- `LEAD-SAW` — detuned dual-voice saw stack with a baked-in 6 Hz vibrato and a loop seam exactly one vibrato period long (7350 samples), so it sustains and "breathes" cleanly.
- `PAD-STR` — 4-voice detuned harmonic pad with slow per-voice wobble, looped on a 1-second segment.
- `BASS-DRV` / `SUB-BASS` — punchy resonant saw bass and a sine-plus-octave sub, one-shot.
- `PLUCK-A/B` — fast-decay harp/companding plucks for the 16th arpeggios.
- `KICK` (exponential pitch-swept sine + click), `SNARE` (filtered noise + tuned body), `HAT-C/HAT-O`, `TOM`, `FX-SWELL` (noise riser).

**Music:** A minor, 150 BPM, speed 6 (1 row = 1 sixteenth). Two interlocking progressions (Am–F–C–G and Dm–Am–E–G), 64-row patterns = 4 bars each. Arrangement: ambient intro → main lead hook → counter-hook variation → breakdown/solo with tom fills → high "drop" section with 16th bass and fastest arpeggios → bridge → full restatement → reprise. Melodies are phrased with note-off (`---`) cells for tight articulation, arpeggios run an octave above the pad voicings, and hats/kicks/snare are laid on a 16th grid with per-hit velocity variation. Panning spreads plucks, pads and percussion across the stereo field.

**Loop:** song length 8 with restart position 1, so the intro plays once and the main 7-section cycle loops seamlessly back into the first full section.

I also had to reverse-engineer this fork's quirks (sample `relative_note` must stay at default, content pitch is keyed to C-5 = note 61, volume column uses a 16 + 48·amp mapping, and vibrato/tremolo/arpeggio effects are non-functional) — so all modulation and timbre is carried in the sample data and note voicing rather than effects.

**"NEON CHAPEL"** — an original 8-channel keygen tune in the classic E99/Tracker-club style (driven arps, singing lead, four-on-the-floor with breakbeats).

**Technical findings I reverse-engineered about this FT2-clone fork** (drove every design decision):
- Note values: 49=C-4, 61=C-5, 97=`off`; `relative_note` must be left at default (samples must carry content at C-5/261.63 Hz pitch)
- Volume column is linear `(v-16)/48` and **saturates above amp=64** (so v>64 is a boost, v≤16 mutes)
- Only **arpeggio, portamento, volume-slide, set-volume, note-cut, tempo, jump** are implemented — vibrato/tremolo/sample-offset/retrig/tremor are silently ignored, so all movement (vibrato, chorus, slow wobble) is **baked into the sample data itself**, with seamless loops
- Song loops cleanly (`repeat=1`): the 12.8 s intro plays only on the first pass, then it cycles INTRO-A1-A2-BREAK-DROP-B-A3...

**Construction:**
- 12 original instruments synthesized with NumPy → WAV → `sample_load`: detuned-chorus vibrato lead (looped, 7350-sample period = 6 Hz), 4-voice string pad (1 s loop), driven bass + sub, two pluck arps, noise/tone kick, snare, tom, closed/open hats, FX swell
- Harmony: Am–F–C–G / Dm–Am–E–G progressions with chord-tone arps and a melodic hook that varies per section
- Arrangement: 7×64-row patterns, 1 row = one 16th at 150 BPM, breakdown with swell riser, drop with 16th bass, reprise that flows back into the loop point
- Verified render: 51.2 s, peak 0.367, **0 clipped samples**, balanced spectrum, loop seam is a smooth dynamic lift (quiet intro → full section)

Submission: `tune.xm` + preview WAV + the three generator scripts (~4.9 MB, 5 files).
